claim: deploy.yml (Deploy to Production)'s workflow_run trigger acts only on this repository's own CI runs on main -- a push, or a manual (workflow_dispatch) run -- as far as a strict text reader can hold it (a direct, writer-only workflow_dispatch of deploy.yml itself runs the stages too, as before). ci-gate carries no job-level if (plain, quoted or spaced key) and one refusal step equal, line for line, to the allowed text: it reads the triggering run's event and head repository through env and exits 1 unless the event is 'push' or 'workflow_dispatch' and the repository is this one (a dispatch from a fork is refused); no line of ci-gate names GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_OUTPUT literally. The on: block, up to the next top-level key, equals the allowed one and no defaults: is set. The jobs: block holds only plain job keys (a quoted, flow-style, anchored or aliased job key, a job-level line that is not a plain lowercase key (quoted, tagged, anchored, explicit or merge key), a five-space indent, an unclosed quoted job-level value, a tab or a duplicate fails), the job set is fixed, and each job's single job-level if (block scalars read with their blank lines, plain scalars with their continuation lines) equals the one allowed: every workflow_run-startable job requires the own-run group (event push or workflow_dispatch, and this repository), rollback-guide is dispatch-only; no job is a reusable-workflow call; nothing sets continue-on-error. Held by scripts/check_deploy_own_pushes.py (gate-owned, run with python3 -I), whose --self-test plants exactly the 52 breaks it lists, including a fork's dispatch, another event type and a missing repository check in a stage if and in the refusal step, and a missing repository check in deploy-audit's if; run by scripts/test_pr_audit_gate.py. Not held: how ci-gate executes, and workflow-level keys other than on: and defaults: -- a job-level key on ci-gate other than if, another step or action in ci-gate, an env/path-file write other than the literal GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_OUTPUT, a workflow-level env (BASH_ENV, BASH_FUNC_*), permissions or run-name, or a column-0 comment inside on: hiding an added trigger all pass the guard (known examples: `concurrency: |` before the refusal step; container, runs-on: self-hosted or services on ci-gate; job-level env: BASH_ENV; workflow-level BASH_FUNC_exit%%, which makes the refusal step exit 0 in local bash; a github-script step exporting BASH_ENV; a GITHUB_PATH or indirect env-file write; ci-gate steps that run what the triggering run controls (checking out head_sha and running a script, running a downloaded artifact of that run, or echoing head_commit.message into a shell); the on: comment). Changes that only alter whether ci-gate goes green are still refused by every stage's and deploy-audit's if, pinned exactly and unchanged. Any ci-gate step that runs, sources, or interpolates into a shell anything the triggering run controls reopens the original exposure. That includes its checkout, its artifacts or caches, and event fields the fork writes, such as head_commit.message and display_title. ci-gate has no if and inherits ADMIN_API_KEY, so only gate ownership stops it. (the class as the round-5 ADR 0090 planner defined it, recorded on the founder's pick "Describe the whole class, then fix the key (Recommended)"; scoping ADMIN_API_KEY out of the workflow env, with permissions: {} and no cache save on ci-gate, is the filed follow-up, since the key alone does not close it: main's GITHUB_TOKEN with actions: write, main-scoped cache writes and other workflow-level secrets remain) (closing the class: tech-debt.d/2026-09-30-batch-open-prs-2026-09-29.md); ci-gate's first step (the conclusion check, pinned separately by ADR-0097's row) and GitHub's own YAML evaluation (a form this reader accepts but GitHub reads differently) (workflow_run runs main's copy, so the step first runs on the merge commit's Deploy run). Founder, 2026-09-30, on #534, verbatim picks: "Sign off, add deploy fix (Recommended)", "Yes, covered (Recommended)" (his sign-off covers the guard and this fragment, 33 gate-owned files), "Honest record (Recommended)" and "Describe the whole class, then fix the key (Recommended)" (this record names what the guard does not hold; he re-confirmed the sign-off on the files it changes) and "Also allow manual runs" (so pr_audit_gate.py's CI-side merge re-entry, a workflow_dispatch of CI on main, still reaches the deploy audit). Recorded as ADR 0097's 2026-09-30 amendment.
